25/G.goal: Describe how human perception and sensory physiology shape the design of XR systems.
25/G.achieves: Provides foundational human-factors knowledge that supports the course aim of understanding and implementing an XR system with confidence.

25/O1.goal: Explain why creating presence in XR requires understanding human perception and how perceptual psychology frames the related design questions, including risks such as cybersickness.
25/O1.achieves: Gives the learner a conceptual basis for recognizing human perceptual constraints and selecting relevant human-factors considerations in later XR design work.

25/O2.goal: Describe how the human senses are organized by stimulus, receptor, and sense organ and why each sensory system responds selectively to specific stimuli.
25/O2.achieves: Gives the learner the sensory-physiological vocabulary needed to understand later XR topics on visual, auditory, and other senses.
